I've been farming this land for 40 years. My mother farmed it before me. I know this soil. I know what it needs.

My land is 10.1 mu. I do wheat in winter, maize in summer on the same plots — that's what everyone around here does, that's what works. My son helps when he can, but he works in the city most of the time. It's mostly me and my husband now, so I have to be careful not to take on more work than we can handle.

For **wheat**, I'll sow in mid-October like always. I buy improved variety seeds from the village supply cooperative — I stopped using my own saved seed years ago when the neighbors' yields started beating mine. I'll do a deep plough this autumn because the soil needs it after summer maize. I'll put down compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress with urea before jointing. Water three times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots, once at jointing, once at heading. I'll spray twice — once for weeds early on, once for aphids before harvest. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

For **maize**, I'll sow right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste, I want the whole growing season. I always use hybrid seed, same brand as my neighbors. Summer maize doesn't need as much water because we get some rain, but I'll pump from the well twice if it's dry. I'll apply urea in two rounds. I don't do much tillage for maize — just rotary to break up the stubble. One pesticide spray for corn borer, maybe two if it's bad. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

I'm not going to change much from last year. What I've been doing feeds my family and gives us a little extra to sell. No reason to experiment at my age.
